app.name: AniFlow
attention.deleteDownloadHint: Throw away the file AniFlow downloaded and keep the one in the library. Only the download folder is touched.
attention.dismissAllConfirm: Dismiss all {n} entries? Nothing is downloaded, moved or deleted.
attention.dismissAllHint: Removes every entry in this list without doing anything about them. Anything whose cause is still there will be raised again.
attention.duplicates: {n} further warning(s) about this episode, collapsed into this row
attention.explain.accept_metadata: Drops the value you set by hand, so this anime follows the metadata source again - now and from now on. Skip it with Dismiss to keep yours.
attention.explain.approve: Downloads this newer version. The old file stays next to it until you choose which one to delete.
attention.explain.assign: You pick which anime this release belongs to. AniFlow then checks the name against that anime's profile: if it fits, the episode is downloaded; if it does not, you are told which rules it failed and nothing else changes.
attention.explain.delete_download: Deletes the downloaded copy in the download folder. The file already in your library is not touched.
attention.explain.delete_newer: Deletes the file the episode uses now and keeps the older copy instead.
attention.explain.delete_older: Deletes the older copy from your library and keeps the file the episode uses now.
attention.explain.dismiss: Removes this entry without doing anything about it. If the cause is still there it will be raised again.
attention.explain.move_now: Moves the finished download into the library now, instead of waiting for the next import pass.
attention.explain.replace_library: Puts the downloaded copy into the library over the file that is there now. The one being replaced is deleted.
attention.explain.retry_now: Hands the torrent to your download client again, right now, instead of waiting for the next automatic pass.
attention.fix.AMBIGUOUS_RELEASE: This release name fits more than one anime in your watchlist. Saying which one writes an alias, so the next one is unambiguous.
attention.fix.DOWNLOAD_MISSING: AniFlow will hand this to your download client again on the next pass, within half an hour.
attention.fix.DOWNLOAD_STALLED: Nobody is seeding this release, so it will not start on its own. Another group will have the episode.
attention.fix.DUPLICATE_FILES: AniFlow keeps both files until you choose. Until then a media server may list the episode twice.
attention.fix.EPISODE_NOT_IDENTIFIABLE: AniFlow knows which anime this is, but could not read a single episode number from the release name below — most often a batch covering a whole season rather than one episode. Nothing is queued for it automatically. Dismiss it if you already have what it covers, or check the name yourself if you think it should be one specific episode.
attention.fix.FEED_FAILED: AniFlow will try this feed again on the next scan. Releases it already found are unaffected.
attention.fix.IMPORT_BLOCKED: The import stopped rather than do something it could not undo. Nothing was moved or deleted.
attention.fix.METADATA_CHANGED: The metadata source has changed a value you had set by hand. Nothing has been overwritten: your value still applies until you decide.
attention.fix.NEEDS_CONVERSION: This entry has no release name yet, so nothing can be matched to it. Choose a release to give it one.
attention.fix.NEW_VERSION: The group re-released this episode. Replacing means downloading and importing again over a file that already plays.
attention.fix.NO_RELEASES: Each search pass now attaches what it finds to the episodes, so this clears itself once the group publishes something that matches. If the group or the quality is wrong rather than the season early, change the release instead — nothing will match until you do.
attention.kindHint.DOWNLOAD_STALLED: The torrent is in your client and connected, and no seeder has sent anything for hours. A release nobody is seeding will not start on its own — changing the subgroup on the anime is the fix.
attention.mediaTranscodeHint: In the library and playable, but the media server has to re-encode it to send it. Choosing another release group fixes it; the file is otherwise fine.
attention.moveNowHint: Hand this downloaded file to the import pass.
attention.noReleasesHint: The indexer answered, and nothing it returned matches this anime's release name. Check the release name against what the group actually publishes under - Change the release will let you pick a real one.
attention.page.hint: Things waiting on a decision. Each one closes itself once its reason goes away, so this list is what is wrong now rather than a history of what once was.
attention.replaceLibraryConfirm: Remove {file} from the library and import the newly downloaded file instead?
attention.replaceLibraryHint: Remove the library's copy — it is what blocks the new one — and let the new file go through the normal import.
attention.summary.AMBIGUOUS_RELEASE: One release name matches more than one anime on your watchlist. Pick which one it belongs to.
attention.summary.DOWNLOAD_MISSING: The torrent is no longer in qBittorrent. AniFlow will hand it over again on the next pass.
attention.summary.DOWNLOAD_STALLED: The torrent is connected and nobody has sent anything for hours.
attention.summary.DUPLICATE_FILES: One episode has two files in your library. Choose which one to delete.
attention.summary.EPISODE_NOT_IDENTIFIAB: AniFlow knows which anime this is, but could not read a single episode number from the release name - most often a batch covering more than one episode.
attention.summary.FEED_FAILED: An RSS source could not be read. The next scan tries again.
attention.summary.IMPORT_BLOCKED: The download finished but the file could not be put into your library.
attention.summary.METADATA_CHANGED: The metadata source now disagrees with a value you set by hand. Yours still applies.
attention.summary.NEEDS_CONVERSION: This entry has no release name yet, so nothing can be matched to it.
attention.summary.NEW_VERSION: A newer version of an episode you already have. Replace it, keep both, or ignore it.
attention.summary.NO_RELEASES: The indexer answered and nothing it returned fits this anime's release profile.

health.missing.episodes_with_a_release: episodes that have something to download
health.missing.episodes_without_a_releas: episodes with nothing to download them
health.missing.fewer_episodes_than_anidb: more episodes on AniDB than here
health.missing.files_not_on_disk: files the episodes claim are not on disk
health.missing.matched_by_name_only: matched to Shoko by name rather than by id
health.missing.releases_for_aired_episod: aired episodes with nothing to download
health.missing.shoko_missing_aired: an aired episode Shoko does not have
health.missing.shoko_missing_episodes: aired episodes Shoko has not got
health.na.no_anidb_id: no AniDB id, so this cannot be compared
health.na.no_indexer: no indexer is configured, so nothing can be downloaded
health.na.not_aired_yet: has not aired yet - nothing to download until its season starts
health.na.not_in_shoko: Shoko Server does not have this
health.na.releases_ignored: You asked for this one to be left alone, so nothing is looking for releases of it.
health.na.shoko_not_answered: Shoko Server has not been asked yet
health.na.tracker_entry: a tracker entry - nothing is downloading it
health.note.import_folder_unused: There is no hand-over folder, and nothing needs one: every file this anime owns arrived some other way - adopted from Shoko, or put there by hand. AniFlow creates the folder the first time it hands Shoko an episode of its own.
health.why.duplicate_files: An original kept by a release change, or an older version, sits next to the episode's own file. AniFlow keeps both until you choose.
health.why.feed_source: Without one, new episodes are only noticed when a search runs.
health.why.fewer_episodes_than_anidb: AniDB lists more episodes than the metadata source gave AniFlow, so “all episodes” here may be short of the real total.
health.why.files_not_on_disk: The episodes say they own a file and it is not where they say. Moved, renamed or deleted outside AniFlow.
health.why.matched_by_name_only: Shoko's entry was found by comparing names, not by AniDB id. Right most of the time, and wrong for a season whose name repeats.
health.why.media_folder: Where this anime's files live. Until it is known, files cannot be found or placed.
health.why.release_name: This is the name releases are published under. Without it nothing can be matched.
health.why.releases_for_aired_episodes: These episodes have aired and there is no magnet for them: nothing published under this release name and subgroup has matched them. They are listed under Found. It does not mean a new episode was missed - an episode that never had a release looks the same here.
health.why.shoko_missing_aired: AniDB gives these episodes an air date in the past and Shoko has no file for them. This is not about AniFlow's own count: if Shoko holds 10 and AniFlow has 10 but AniDB lists 13, it says episode 11 aired and nobody has it.
health.why.subgroup: Which group's release to take. Without one, any group's is as good as another's.

import.reason.duplicate_episode: This version is already here or downloading - nothing was downloaded
import.reason.duplicate_of_another_row: Another download row already has this exact torrent - that one is the download, this row is a leftover
import.reason.episode_not_identifiable: The episode number could not be read from the name

import.reason.import_root_missing: No import folder is mounted, so there is nowhere to hand the file over
import.reason.media_folder_missing: This anime has no library folder yet - set one in Configuration
import.reason.missing_in_client: qBittorrent no longer has this torrent — it may have been cleaned up after finishing, or removed by hand
import.reason.new_version_needs_review: A newer version was found. Approve it to replace the episode.
import.reason.no_media_found: No video file found in download
import.reason.not_aired_yet: Its season has not started yet.
import.reason.path_outside_root: File is outside the allowed download folder
import.reason.qb_not_configured: qBittorrent is not configured, so this was never handed over
import.reason.ready_to_move: Downloaded and waiting to be moved into the library
import.reason.releases_ignored: You asked for this one to be left alone, so nothing is looking for releases of it.
import.reason.shoko_file_gone: Shoko Server took the file but it never appeared in the library - it may have treated it as a duplicate
import.reason.shoko_not_imported: Waiting on Shoko Server — still in the import folder, often a release AniDB does not know yet
import.reason.skipped_anidb_list: Your AniDB list says you have this episode, so it is not fetched. Press Download on it, or fetch them all from the release panel.
import.reason.not_in_anidb_list: Your AniDB list has the other episodes of this anime but not this one, and no release has been found for it either.
import.reason.source_missing: The downloaded file is not where AniFlow left it. It retries every pass, so a torrent client that was briefly unreachable fixes itself — nothing to do unless this stays.
import.reason.source_unknown: AniFlow does not know which file this download produced yet. It retries every pass and usually resolves once the client reports the finished torrent.
import.reason.superseded_version: Older than the version you already have - nothing was downloaded
import.reason.target_exists: This episode is already in your library
import.reason.tracker_entry: This entry was added with no indexer configured, so there is nothing to search.
indexer.deleteConfirm: Delete “{name}”? Its file is removed too, and searching stops until another indexer is added.
indexer.emptyBody: Until there is one, AniFlow cannot search: adding an anime finds nothing, and the watchlist has only what your feeds bring in. Copy example.yaml in the folder above to a real name and edit it.
indexer.howToAdd: Put a YAML file for each site in this folder. AniFlow picks it up straight away - no restart, no import. A file named example.yaml is ignored; it shows the format.
indexer.shipsNone: AniFlow ships with no indexers - it’s up to you to find and provide your own, as we cannot provide them.
indexer.title: Indexer
inspector.addTermHint: Add this term to the list below and switch to Custom, clearing the box so the same word is never searched twice.
inspector.cancelHint: Stop after the term being asked now. What has been found so far is kept.
inspector.clearSymbolsHint: Replaces the characters no release group types and no tracker indexes - stars, hearts, colons, underscores and the like - with spaces. "Hetalia World★Stars (2026)" becomes "Hetalia World Stars (2026)".
inspector.filterQualityHint: Its own box: the one beside it matches tags the parser recognised, and a resolution is a field of its own.
inspector.filterTagHint: Matched against what the parser recognised — source, codecs, version, CRC and the tags it saw but could not classify.
inspector.groupedHint: The same hits, grouped by subgroup and quality the way the add-anime step groups them, with the filters above applied.
inspector.modeHint.custom: {n} requests - the box, if it holds a term, and everything in the list below, each read for as many pages as set there.
inspector.modeHint.full: {n} requests. Quick's own two searches, plus the whole cleaned name of everything AniFlow holds, read to the end - so nothing a release group might have typed is missed.
inspector.modeHint.japanese: {n} requests, every page of each. The Japanese title in the tracker's non-English category and the best Latin spelling in the ordinary one.
inspector.modeHint.quick: {n} requests, one page each. English and Romaji, cleaned and cut to their first four words - the fastest question that still finds a well-named release.
inspector.nameMissing: The metadata source has no such name for this anime.
inspector.nativeHint: Trackers that file releases by the language they were translated into keep Japanese-named releases somewhere else. A Japanese title searched in the English-translated category finds nothing at all — not because the release is missing, but because it was never there. The Japanese button switches this on for you.
inspector.noIndexer: There is no indexer configured, so there is nothing to search.
inspector.noListing: This indexer's definition has no search page, so the search read the site's feed - which on some sites serves one page and ignores the page number, whatever it is asked for. Add these two lines to config/indexers/{file} on the deployment (the config folder is yours, so a new build never overwrites it):
inspector.noTotal: This indexer's definition does not say where the site states its own result count, so "the site says" stays a dash. Add total_url and total_pattern to config/indexers/{file} on the deployment.
inspector.pagesHint: How many pages of the tracker's results each custom term reads.
inspector.pickFirst: Pick a show above to search for it.
inspector.pickRow: Pick a group to see what it has, episode by episode.
inspector.repeatedHint: The indexer answered the next page with the page before it, so the walk stopped. This feed cannot be paged, and anything past the first page is out of reach.
inspector.rowsHint: The groups this search found, exactly as the Choose release window lists them. Pick one to see its files - nothing is picked for you, so no request is spent on a row nobody asked about.
inspector.searchPlaceholder: The name to search the indexer for
inspector.seasonHint: The same line-up the Calendar draws. Picking one here only says what to search for - nothing is added and no window opens.
inspector.termFoundHint: Rows the indexer handed back for this term, duplicates included. Two pages of 75 are 150 whether or not they held the same files.
inspector.termNewHint: How many of those were releases nothing had returned before - what this term actually contributed.
inspector.termPagesHint: How many times the indexer was asked for this term: one per page, plus one for the site's own count.
inspector.termSiteHint: How many results the site itself reports for this search, read from its own search page. A dash means its definition file does not say where that number is.
inspector.termTimeHint: How long this term took on the server, the pause before it included. The mode that finds the most is not always the one worth waiting for.
inspector.termsHint: Read the last two columns together: the site's own count against what came back. They should be close, and a large gap means the search is not reaching what is there.
inspector.warning: A debug view. Nothing on this page adds, changes or downloads anything — it shows what the indexer returned and what AniFlow made of it.

anidb.page.hint: What AniFlow knows from AniDB: the title list it downloads and the My List export you upload. AniFlow never asks AniDB itself.
anidb.export.title: My List export
anidb.export.hint: Your AniDB My List, from the export file you upload. AniFlow keeps a copy in its data folder, so a new feature can read it again without another upload.
anidb.export.reupload: This export was uploaded before AniFlow kept a copy, so the newer tabs (Not watched, State unknown, Several groups) cannot read it. Upload it once more - from now on AniFlow reads its own copy again by itself.
anidb.noExport: No export uploaded yet. Upload it on the Library tab.
anidb.incomplete.hint: Your My List, filtered the way AniDB's own My List page filters. Anime that are only on the account, with nothing in the list, are not incomplete.
anidb.unwatched.hint: Episodes you have on disk that nobody marked as watched on AniDB. An episode counts as watched when any of its files is.
anidb.unknown.hint: Episodes with a file whose My List state is unknown - AniDB does not know where the file is.
anidb.groups.hint: Anime with files from more than one release group. The export names a group by AniDB's number, not by its name; the number opens the group on AniDB.
anidb.groups.doubled: Only where one episode is held twice, from two groups
anidb.empty: Nothing here ({n} anime in the export).

profile.matched: Match — this release follows your rules
profile.notMatched: No match — this release violates your rules

profiles.deleteConfirm: Delete this template? Anime using it keep their copied settings.
profiles.deleteInUse: It is currently used by {n} anime.
profiles.emptyBody: Create reusable rules - a release group and a resolution - and apply them to every anime with two clicks.
profiles.error: The template could not be saved. Please try again.
release.keepWarning: Both versions stay in your library, so a media server will list this episode twice. You will be asked which one to delete.
rss.sources.hint: Add an RSS feed for a subgroup to let AniFlow automatically download their latest releases.
profiles.favoriteHint: Favorite release groups are shown first in search results to help you find them faster.
profiles.name: Template name
profiles.seededHint: Pre-filled from what the search found. Everything is editable - just give the template a name.
profiles.testNoFeed: No feed could be read, so this says nothing about the profile
profiles.testNoGroup: Your feeds carry nothing from {groups} — check the spelling of the group name
profiles.testNoMatch: The group is publishing, but nothing passes
profiles.testOk: Would take {n} of the {total} releases in your feeds right now
progress.archiveHint: Episodes that finished cleanly, or that you archived by hand. Read-only - nothing here can still be acted on.
progress.deleteAllConfirm: Delete the downloaded copy for {n} episodes? The files already in your library are not touched.
progress.explainDismiss: Move this to the Archive. It comes back here if anything about it changes again.
progress.hint: Every episode currently moving through AniFlow, or stuck on something - one card per episode, updated in place.
progress.runImportHint: Shoko files new files on its own schedule, which can be a long time apart. This is the same as pressing Run Import in Shoko - it usually clears a file that is waiting or not found.
progress.importStarted: Shoko is running its import now. Give it a minute, then check back - this page updates by itself.
progress.importFailed: Shoko could not be asked to run its import.
progress.replaceAllConfirm: Replace the library copy for {n} episodes with the newly downloaded files? The files being replaced are deleted.
progress.title: In Progress
progress.waiting: AniFlow is working on this by itself - nothing to press yet.
release.fixHint: Corrects what AniFlow knows about this anime. Nothing here deletes, renames or replaces a file.
release.fixMissingHint: Look for the episodes this anime is missing and download them. Nothing already in the library is touched, and nothing is deleted.
release.skippedTitle: {n} episodes are skipped because your AniDB list has them.
release.skippedHint: They are not downloaded on their own. This makes them wanted like any other missing episode.
release.ignoreHint: No searching, no downloads, no warnings. Your files stay as they are.
release.leftoversHint: Renamed to .backup by an earlier release change and left on disk. AniFlow does not touch these - deleting them is yours to decide.
release.matchOnlyHint: Searches for this anime and writes down the release name, group and quality it is already in - without downloading anything. Worth doing for a library that came from somewhere else, so a later v2 or v3 can be recognised.
release.noHigher: There is nothing above the current quality.
release.noLower: There is nothing below the current quality.
release.nothingOwned: No episodes are in the library yet, so there is nothing to replace.
release.title: Change the release
rss.deleteConfirm: Delete this feed source? Already discovered releases are kept.
rss.error: The RSS service could not be reached. Please try again.
rss.info.hint: What the scheduler is doing, and what each feed has produced.
rss.info.perFeedHint: A feed with discoveries but no matches is being read fine - its items just never belong to anything on your watchlist.
rss.info.title: RSS automation
rss.info.workerOff: Not running - nothing is scanned on a schedule
rss.releases.clearConfirm: Clear all {n} discovered releases from the list? Nothing is downloaded or deleted, and pending downloads keep their place.
rss.releases.clearHint: Empties the list. The feed still remembers these items, so they are not reported as new finds again.
rss.releases.empty: No releases discovered yet. Add a feed and run a scan.
rss.releases.hint: What your watchlist matched or was offered and turned down, newest first, up to the last 150.
rss.releases.title: Discovered releases
rss.sources.empty: No feeds configured yet. Add an RSS feed so AniFlow can watch for releases.
rss.sources.title: Feed sources
rss.status.noFeeds: No enabled feed. Add one below so scanning has something to read.
rss.status.title: RSS automation
samples.failed: That did not work. Debug mode has to be on.
samples.hint: Creates one record of every kind - every attention type and every activity entry - so the look, the wording and the buttons can all be checked without waiting for something to go wrong. No anime, episode or download is created, so an action button on a sample will usually fail; that it is there, and says what it will do, is the point.
samples.title: Sample records
scan.absolute: Numbered {first}–{last}: this group counts from the start of the series, not from this season
scan.absoluteHint: Some groups restart at 1 each season and write the season into the name; others keep counting. Both are correct, but the episode numbers will be the ones you see here. Pick the other group if you want 1–12.
scan.alsoSeen: Also seen, and why it was left out
scan.duplicates: {n} episode(s) still have more than one file: {list}. Those are repacks or genuine duplicates — the editions are already split into their own rows.
scan.empty.no-episode: Only batches — no single episodes to pick from
scan.empty.no-indexer: No indexer configured — nothing to search
scan.empty.no-title: The names carry no title AniFlow can use
scan.empty.nothing-found: This group has nothing for this name
scan.empty.other-show: What came back belongs to another season or show
scan.empty.profile: Found, but your group or quality rules refuse all of it
scan.empty.unreadable: The names could not be read
scan.onlyOneNameFound: Only “{name}” found anything — keep the other names in the search.
schedule.column.name: Name
schedule.dot.error: The last run failed - click to see why
schedule.hint: Everything that runs on its own, and when.
schedule.resetAllConfirm: Reset every task's own switch and interval back to the default? Anything you changed on this page is lost.
schedule.tasks.anidb_identity_refresh.de: Keeps the AniDB title dump and the offline id-mapping list current, and gives newly-added anime their AniDB id. Never fetched more than once a week, however low this interval is set — a ban from asking too often is installation-wide and permanent-feeling.
schedule.tasks.attention_review.descript: Checks every open attention warning and closes the ones whose reason has gone away, so the list only ever shows something that still needs a look.
schedule.tasks.attention_review.name: Watchlist: Clearing resolved warnings
schedule.tasks.calendar_auto_update.desc: Refreshes the current season, the next two and the one before, the same as the "Update upcoming" button — only when nothing is already running. Unconditional: once a week is rare enough that there is no "is it stale yet" question worth checking first.
schedule.tasks.calendar_auto_update.name: Calendar: Keeping the current + 2 next seasons up to date
schedule.tasks.conversion_review.descrip: Flags anime that were added without an indexer and now need converting, since an indexer can appear later by someone dropping a file into a folder, with nothing else announcing it.
schedule.tasks.conversion_review.name: Watchlist: Checking for indexer setup needed
schedule.tasks.disk_recheck.description: Re-checks every anime's linked media folder against the database — the same check a manual Rescan does, just for the whole library on its own timer. Catches a file moved, renamed or deleted by something other than AniFlow's own download pipeline, which nothing else here would notice.
schedule.tasks.disk_recheck.name: Library: Re-checking files on disk
schedule.tasks.metadata_backfill.descrip: Looks up whatever is still missing for watchlist entries — airing schedule, genres, studio, synopsis — a few at a time. Most useful right after a library is adopted from Shoko, where this has the most to fill in; does nothing once every entry is complete. Manual only.
schedule.tasks.metadata_backfill.name: Watchlist: Filling in missing details
schedule.tasks.metadata_status.descripti: Notices the metadata provider (AniList or Kitsu) coming back online or going away. Manual only — press Run for a current answer.
schedule.tasks.metadata_status.name: Watchlist: Checking metadata provider availability
schedule.tasks.queue_downloads.descripti: Hands matched releases to the torrent client, including anything the client refused earlier and anything an Automate switch made available since the last pass. Runs automatically right after a feed scan, and manually from here or the Downloads page.
schedule.tasks.queue_downloads.name: RSS: Queuing matched releases
schedule.tasks.rss_scan.description: Reads every enabled RSS feed for releases that match your watchlist, then queues whatever it finds — the same thing the Scan now button on RSS Sources does.
schedule.tasks.rss_scan.name: RSS: Scanning feeds for new episodes
schedule.tasks.anime_search.description: Searches every configured indexer for releases matching anime on your watchlist. Manual only — nothing searches on its own timer.
schedule.tasks.anime_search.name: Downloads: Searching for releases
schedule.tasks.shoko_adoption.descriptio: Adopts anime and episodes Shoko Server already holds that are not yet on the watchlist, and fills in details for ones that are. Manual only — the same button lives on the Shoko Server page.
schedule.tasks.shoko_adoption.name: Shoko: Importing Shoko's library
schedule.tasks.shoko_status.description: Notices Shoko Server coming back online or going away, so the rest of the app knows without waiting for something else to fail first.
schedule.tasks.shoko_status.name: Shoko: Checking Shoko availability
schedule.tasks.torrent_monitor.descripti: Asks the torrent client how every download is progressing, imports whatever has finished, and — in Shoko Server mode — looks for files Shoko has since placed. A finished download is settled with the client right away if this pass is the one that imported it. Ticks every 5 seconds while something is actually downloading; the configured interval is how often it checks while idle.
schedule.tasks.torrent_monitor.name: Downloads: Syncing download status
schedule.tasks.torrent_housekeeping.desc: Adopts finished torrents in AniFlow's category that no download row knows about, and reconciles every unsettled download against the client, disk and library — is it in the client under another category, is the file already on disk, is the episode already in the library. Settling a torrent the import step never got to only happens when this is run by hand.
schedule.tasks.torrent_housekeeping.name: Downloads: Housekeeping
schedule.title: Schedule
settings.accountHint: Fill in only what you want to change: a username on its own renames the account, a new password on its own replaces the password. Either way your current password is required — otherwise anyone at an unlocked browser could lock you out of your own AniFlow.
settings.afterImportHint: Pausing stops seeding but keeps the torrent listed, so you can see that AniFlow noticed the download finished. Files are never deleted.
settings.appModeHint: AniFlow decides this from whether an indexer is configured: with none it cannot download anything, so it hides everything about downloading and works as a watchlist and calendar. The override is for trying the other mode without adding or removing an indexer, and will be removed.
settings.calendar.kindsHint: Anything not listed here is shown, so a kind a source invents next year appears rather than quietly vanishing. Music videos, adverts and trailers are hidden by default — there are hundreds of them in a season.
settings.calendar.markSequels: Mark seasons of shows you already track
settings.calendar.markSequelsHint: A later season of something in your watchlist is outlined and lifted up the list. A season you appear to have skipped is marked more strongly — nobody skips a middle season on purpose.
settings.calendar.showPopularityHint: One to five stars, relative to the season on screen rather than a fixed number — a quiet season still has a most-watched show.
settings.configFileHint: You can edit it with any text editor - AniFlow picks up changes without a restart, and saving here rewrites the file.
settings.debugLogSent: Sent four lines — check the log now
settings.error: Settings could not be saved. Please try again.
settings.fileOperation.copy: Copy (keep the download, can keep seeding)
settings.fileOperation.move: Move (the download folder gives the file up)
settings.fileOperation.shokoserver: Getting the file to Shoko Server
settings.fileOperation.standalone: Getting the file into the library
settings.fileOperationHint: Copy leaves the episode on disk twice and lets the torrent keep seeding; the download folder then needs occasional cleanup. Move keeps exactly one copy and frees the space immediately.
settings.logLevel.DEBUG: Debug — everything, including each outgoing request
settings.logLevel.WARNING: Warning — failures and things worth knowing
settings.logOptionsHint: Applies to the running app - no restart needed. DEBUG writes a great deal of it.
settings.metadataHint: Where covers, titles, episode counts and airing times come from. One at a time: the two sources use different ids, so mixing them would leave half the library unable to refresh. Switching clears the cached calendar and rebuilds it from the new source — anime already added keep the ids they were added with.
settings.metadataNote.anilist: Airing times, genres and episode counts. Occasionally unreachable, which is what the calendar cache is for.
settings.metadataNote.kitsu: Independent of AniList and MyAnimeList. No broadcast times and no genres, so the calendar shows less.
settings.mode.shokoserver: Shoko Server - Shoko owns the library
settings.modeHint.shokoserver: AniFlow puts finished downloads in the import folder. Shoko Server identifies, renames and moves them into the library, and AniFlow then finds where each file went.
settings.modeHint.standalone: AniFlow places finished downloads in the media library itself, under the folder name stored for each anime.
settings.modeWarning: Chosen once in the setup wizard and recorded when this library was created. Changing it would split every anime across two folders, so it cannot be changed afterwards.
settings.monitorIntervalMoved: How often each task runs is set on the Schedule page.
settings.moveForcedRemove: Switched to “Remove the torrent entry”: a moved file cannot seed.
settings.moveSeedingHint: Moving takes the file away from the torrent, so seeding cannot continue — “Leave it seeding” is unavailable while Move is selected.
settings.password.stored: Password stored — enter a new one to change
settings.pathsHint: The folders on your server, as mounted into AniFlow. Set in docker-compose.yml; changing one needs a redeploy.
settings.proxyDirect: direct — the proxy is not in use
settings.proxyHint: Sends AniFlow's own internet requests - metadata sources, and your indexers and feeds - through a proxy, so those services see the proxy's address instead of yours. Your download client, Shoko and anything else on your own network always go direct.
settings.proxyTorrentWarning: This does not hide your torrent traffic. That traffic belongs to qBittorrent and never passes through AniFlow — set a proxy in qBittorrent itself for that.
settings.rssEnabledHint: When off, use 'Scan now' on the Downloads page to fetch manually.
settings.shokoHint: Optional, and only for reading: AniFlow hands files to Shoko through folders and needs none of this. With an API key it can also read what Shoko knows — series, episodes, and the files it could not identify. The key is Shoko's own API key from its settings; AniFlow never asks for your Shoko password.
settings.shokoKeySet: API key is set (leave empty to keep)
settings.about.databaseBehind: - behind: this build expects {head}. A migration may have failed; look at the log from the start.
settings.about.sourcesHint: Anime information comes from AniList and Kitsu, and optionally Jikan, MyAnimeList and Shikimori; alternative titles from the AniDB title dump, and the id mapping from the anime-lists project. AniFlow is independent and not affiliated with or endorsed by any of them, nor by Shoko or the download clients.
settings.about.privacy: What AniFlow contacts is listed under Privacy in the README.
settings.diagnosticsHint: One file for a bug report: these settings, the Checks, your libraries and indexers, the scheduled tasks, how much is in the database, the last Activity entries and AniFlow's own last log lines. Passwords, keys and tokens are removed; the database and your AniDB export are not in it. Anime titles and folder paths are, because they are in the log - open the file and read it before you send it.
settings.status.pending: Changes not saved yet - they save when you leave the field.
settings.status.error: Could not save the last change.
settings.status.proxyHeld: Saved - except the proxy, which is not saved until it has a host and a port.
settings.metadataConfirm: Switching the calendar's source clears the calendar and rebuilds it, and the two sources use different ids. Switch anyway?
settings.downloads.pathsHint: AniFlow asks the torrent client where it saves, translates that to the path AniFlow sees, and checks that it can read the download folder and write the library. Uses the client address and login above, saved or not.
settings.tv.title: AniFlow TV
settings.tv.hint: Each television gets its own token. A TV can read the watchlist, the schedule, the calendar and In Progress, and add a show to the watchlist - nothing else. Revoke a token to cut that TV off.
settings.tv.name: Name of this TV
settings.tv.tokenHint: Shown once - AniFlow keeps only a fingerprint of it. Enter it, with the address below, in AniFlow TV's Settings.
settings.tv.pair.button: Pair a TV with a code
settings.tv.pair.buttonHint: Easiest: the TV shows a QR code - scan it with your phone, or type the code here.
settings.tv.pair.title: Pair a TV
settings.tv.pair.hint: Enter the code your TV is showing. AniFlow gives that TV its own token - you never have to type it.
settings.tv.pair.unknown: That code is not waiting for an answer. It may have run out (codes last five minutes) - start again on the TV.
settings.tv.pair.found: A TV is asking to connect. If the code above is the one on your screen, approve it.
settings.tv.pair.recognised: AniFlow recognises this TV: it is "{name}" (last used {when}). That entry is replaced by the new one when the TV signs in, so you still have one entry for it.
settings.tv.pair.sameName: Older entries with this name - they may be this same TV. Tick the ones to replace:
settings.tv.pair.done: Paired. The TV signs itself in within a few seconds.
settings.themeFolder: Your own themes go in {folder}. Each needs a theme.yaml stating themes_api: {version}, which is the theme format this build reads.
settings.themesHint: One theme is a folder with a theme.yaml in it. Copy a built-in one to start your own; what a theme leaves out keeps AniFlow's own value.
settings.timezoneUnresolved: This server does not know the timezone “{name}”, so times are in UTC. Check the spelling against the IANA list (Europe/Berlin, not CEST).
settings.titleDisplayHint: What the Calendar and the Watchlist call an anime. Display only — it renames no folder and changes no search. A show with no title of the first kind falls through to the next.
settings.titleFolderHint: Applies where AniFlow names the folder: your library in standalone mode, and the hand-over folder in Shoko Server mode. Shoko names your library itself, so this does not change it.
settings.titleSearchHint: Release groups name files in romaji almost everywhere, so putting English first will usually find less.
settings.titlesHint: A provider gives several names for the same show. These decide which one AniFlow uses, best first — anything lower down is still used when the one above is missing.
settings.toastTestError: This is what a problem looks like.
settings.toastTestMessage: This is what a notification looks like.
settings.toastsHint: Short messages confirming what just happened. They disappear on their own — four seconds for a confirmation, eight for a failure — and clicking one dismisses it early. Nothing ever asks you to press OK.
settings.torrentBehaviour: What happens after a download finishes
settings.delugeHint: Deluge is reached through its Web UI (usually port 8112), not the daemon port. AniFlow files its downloads under a Deluge label, so the Label plugin has to be on - AniFlow switches it on if it can. Deluge has no tags: AniFlow follows its torrents by hash.
settings.delugePassword: Web UI password (the default is deluge)
settings.transmissionHint: Transmission is reached at its RPC address (usually port 9091, e.g. http://transmission:9091). The username and password are only needed if you set them in Transmission. AniFlow marks its torrents with labels, which need Transmission 3.00 or newer.
client.missingTitle: No torrent client is set up.
client.missingBody: Downloads are queued but nothing is sent anywhere until AniFlow can reach one.
setup.account.already: This AniFlow already has an account, and you are signed in.
setup.account.code: AniFlow prints this code in the container log on first start. It cannot be filtered by log level. Only this code can create the first account, preventing others from claiming it.
setup.account.lede: AniFlow runs on your network, so it uses its own login instead of trusting anyone who reaches the port.
setup.account.rules: 8 characters or more. AniFlow has no email address. If you lose your password, Forgot your password prints a new code to the same log. Codes expire after one hour.
setup.account.title: Create your account
setup.resultFilter: Filter results: name, quality, anything else
setup.cancelSearchHint: Stop after the name being asked now. Everything found so far stays on the list.
setup.connections.lede: Connect the services AniFlow uses. Test them now or configure them later in Settings.
setup.connections.shokoNote: AniFlow reads from Shoko and writes to the hand-over folder.
setup.connections.title: The programs AniFlow talks to
setup.error: That did not work. Please try again.
setup.feeds.lede: A feed lets AniFlow notice releases minutes after they are posted, instead of waiting for the next search. Your indexer may already provide one.
setup.feeds.none: None yet. Your indexer stands one up by itself once it is in place.
setup.feeds.optionalBody: Feeds let AniFlow receive new releases as they are published. Without one, releases are only found when you start a search yourself - AniFlow never searches an indexer on its own.
setup.feeds.title: Where new episodes are noticed
setup.filesWaiting: Pick a release above to see its files here.
setup.futureNote: This show has not aired yet - it premieres on {date}. Nothing has been published for it, so there is nothing to match: it is added with everything known about it, and AniFlow will offer to set up its releases once the season starts.
setup.hint.account: Fill in the code and your account details to continue
setup.hint.shoko: Add the Shoko details, or skip this for now
setup.indexerUnreachable: The indexer could not be searched, so this is not a result - it is a failure. Check the indexer settings and that the site is reachable, then try again.
setup.matchNothing: Nothing changed - it already said all of that.
setup.matchResult: Written down: {fields}. {matched} release(s) matched to episodes.
setup.indexerOnlyOne: Only one indexer is switched on, so there is nothing to choose between. Turn more on in Settings.
setup.noAnidbTitle: The calendar has no AniDB id for this show, so there is no AniDB page to open. An id can be added in Edit once it is known.
setup.noDefaultSource: No default RSS feed source is set up yet.
setup.noDefaultTemplate: No default subgroup/quality template is set up yet.
setup.noIndexer: No indexer is configured, so there is nothing to search. Add one on the Indexer Profiles page - you can still add this anime and let your feeds find its episodes.
seed.dead: No seeders - nobody is sharing this right now
seed.unknown: The tracker did not say how many are sharing this
setup.otherGroupHas: In these results {group} {quality} also has {n} episodes this row lacks: {list}
setup.storedRules: This anime's stored profile also applies, whatever the boxes above say: {rules}. Change it in the anime's Edit window.
setup.noneFound: Nothing found for this combination. Try a different subgroup or quality.
setup.numbering.resolveHint: Ask Shoko Server, which keeps AniDB's episode counts - including for seasons you do not have. Nothing is added to your library.
setup.numbering.unknown: Nothing could work this out. Type the number of the first episode of this season.
setup.hint.client: Add the client's address, or skip this for now
setup.client.title: Your torrent client
setup.client.lede: AniFlow hands every download to one torrent client. Pick yours, add its address and login, then test the connection and the download folder.
setup.client.body.deluge: Web UI, port {port} by default. Needs the Web UI password only.

setup.terms.s1.title: What AniFlow is
setup.terms.s1.body: AniFlow is free software that you run yourself, on your own hardware. It keeps a watchlist of the anime you follow, looks for releases on the feeds and search sites that you add, passes the ones that match your own rules to your own torrent client (qBittorrent, Deluge or Transmission), and files finished downloads into your library. Every rule is yours: AniFlow does not decide what you watch or where you get it from.
setup.terms.s2.title: What AniFlow does not do
setup.terms.s2.body: AniFlow does not host, store, upload or distribute any films, series or other copyrighted works, and it does not include any list of sites, feeds, indexers or links to such works. It does not download the media files itself: the transfer is carried out by your own torrent client. AniFlow may fetch small torrent files or magnet links from the sites you have added, so that it can pass them to your client. The sites, the feeds and the torrents are chosen by you.
setup.terms.s3.title: Services AniFlow contacts
setup.terms.s3.body: To fill in titles, episode counts, release dates and cover images, AniFlow contacts public information services: AniList and Kitsu by default, Jikan, MyAnimeList and Shikimori if you switch them on, AniDB (its published title list, at most once a week) and a public id-mapping list on GitHub. It also contacts the sites you add yourself. Those services receive a request from the computer that runs AniFlow, which includes its network address and what is being looked up. If you set a proxy, the requests go through it. AniFlow is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by any of these services or their owners; their names and logos belong to them, and their own terms of use apply to your use of them.
setup.terms.s4.title: Your data
setup.terms.s4.body: AniFlow does not collect, analyse or send information about you or about how you use it. It has no analytics, no telemetry, no crash reports, no update check and no account with its author. Your watchlist, settings, passwords and keys stay on your own machine, in the folders you gave it; the settings file keeps them as plain text, so protect that folder. The only things that leave your machine are the requests described above and the requests to services you set up yourself, such as your torrent client or media server. The diagnostics file is created only when you download it, and AniFlow never sends it anywhere. The author of AniFlow receives none of your data.
